claims.notes: Host-conformance fixtures cover layout, painting and interaction contracts. A general headless user-application UI runner was not established.

claims.name: Documentation and examples
claims.notes: Public documentation, framework guides and example applications are provided.

claims.name: Fractional scaling
claims.notes: The Winit shell combines the floating-point display scale with a custom scale and updates layout when it changes. Not execution-validated across platforms.

claims.name: Pixel snapping
claims.notes: Freya does not support pixel snapping.

claims.name: Fractional scaling
claims.notes: Layout explicitly handles fractional display scales such as 125% and 150%, converting between logical and device pixels. Not execution-validated across platforms.

claims.name: Pixel snapping
claims.notes: Layout snaps authored metrics and resolved box edges in device-pixel space before returning logical bounds.

claims.name: Fractional scaling
claims.notes: The window integration multiplies the floating-point system scale by an arbitrary user scale and updates the context. Not execution-validated across platforms.

claims.name: Pixel snapping
claims.notes: The layout cache rounds relative x/y positions, but preserves widths and heights. This is not a complete shared-edge snapping policy.

claims.name: Fractional scaling
claims.notes: The Winit integration combines floating-point window and application scales and updates the viewport on scale changes. Not execution-validated across platforms.

claims.name: Pixel snapping
claims.notes: Quads expose a snap flag for pixel-grid alignment. Its default follows the crisp feature, so snapping is configurable rather than unconditional for every primitive.

claims.name: Fractional scaling
claims.notes: The official Winit integration stores the native display scale as floating-point pixels per point and updates it on scale changes. Not execution-validated across platforms.

claims.name: Pixel snapping
claims.notes: GuiRounding provides scale-aware rounding to physical pixel boundaries and pixel centers for scalar and geometry types.

claims.name: Fractional scaling
claims.notes: The Winit backend explicitly accounts for fractional display scales when converting requested logical window sizes to physical pixels. Not execution-validated across platforms.

claims.name: Pixel snapping
claims.notes: The FemtoVG renderer snaps text selection x coordinates and text y coordinates when the transform permits it. Framework-wide box-edge snapping across renderers was not established.

claims.name: Fractional scaling
claims.notes: The window integration uses the floating-point OS scale to convert surface dimensions and initialize rendering. Not execution-validated across platforms.

claims.name: Pixel snapping
claims.notes: Taffy layout rounding is explicitly disabled. No replacement framework-wide physical-pixel snapping policy was established in the reviewed source.

claims.name: Fractional scaling
claims.notes: The Blitz shell passes floating-point Winit scale changes into the document viewport's HiDPI scale. Not execution-validated across platforms.

claims.name: Pixel snapping
claims.notes: Blitz rounds resolved layout box edges before painting while preserving unrounded text origins for subpixel text placement.

claims.name: Fractional scaling
claims.notes: The Wayland backend implements the fractional-scale protocol and handles the compositor's preferred scale. Not execution-validated across platforms.

claims.name: Pixel snapping
claims.notes: The Finish shader helpers include a function to snap an edge to whole device pixels. Automatic framework-wide layout snapping was not established.

claims.name: Fractional scaling
claims.notes: The Wayland backend implements preferred fractional-scale events, and layout handles non-integer device scales. Not execution-validated across platforms.

claims.name: Pixel snapping
claims.notes: Layout snaps authored metrics and resolved box edges in device-pixel space before returning logical bounds.

claims.name: Fractional scaling
claims.notes: The Winit web platform handles floating-point scale changes and resizes its rendering surface accordingly. Native-platform parity was not execution-validated.

claims.name: Pixel snapping
claims.notes: Paint-time snapping aligns box edges, borders and clips to device pixels while keeping layout fractional. Moving or rotated content has explicit exceptions, and subtrees can opt out.

claims.name: Fractional scaling
claims.notes: Source regression tests cover surface coverage at 1.2x and 1.25x and pointer hit testing at fractional scales. These tests were source-reviewed, not run here.

claims.name: Pixel snapping
claims.notes: Layout, painting and hit testing share a device-pixel policy for edge rounding, covering bounds and nonzero stroke widths.

claims.name: Fractional scaling
claims.notes: The desktop event loop carries the floating-point Winit display scale into layout and rendering. Not execution-validated across platforms.

claims.name: Pixel snapping
claims.notes: Scroll offsets are rounded in device-pixel space. A framework-wide shared-edge snapping policy for all layout boxes was not established.

claims.name: Fractional scaling
claims.notes: The desktop host passes the floating-point display scale and logical viewport dimensions to the style environment. Not execution-validated across platforms.

claims.name: Pixel snapping
claims.notes: Layout disables Taffy rounding. No replacement framework-wide device-pixel snapping policy was established in the reviewed source.

review.scope: Development-branch source snapshots, not the older versions pinned by benchmark adapters. Features were source-reviewed, not execution-tested on every platform.
review.method: Read repository documentation, manifests, API implementations, examples and regression tests at immutable commits. Built-in means a provided API, not specification completeness. Partial records a specific limitation or specialized scope. Different model identifies delegated/browser/low-level contracts. Unknown means the review did not establish the capability, not that it is absent. Unsupported requires an explicit source statement.
